hello-polite.meaningNote: Polite morning or afternoon greeting; "po" shows respect toward elders or strangers.

good-morning.exampleSentence: Magandang umaga po, kumusta po kayo?

good-evening.meaningNote: Greeting used after sunset or once evening falls.
good-evening.exampleSentence: Magandang gabi po, may bakanteng mesa pa po ba?

how-are-you.meaningNote: Derived from Spanish "¿Cómo está?". "Kayo" is the plural or polite singular pronoun.

nice-to-meet-you.meaningNote: Traditional, highly respectful expression when meeting someone new.
nice-to-meet-you.exampleSentence: Ikinagagalak ko po kayong makilala, Ginoong Ramos.

thank-you-very-much.meaningNote: Standard warm expression of gratitude in Filipino culture.
thank-you-very-much.exampleSentence: Maraming salamat po sa inyong tulong.

you-are-welcome.meaningNote: Reply to thanks meaning "it is nothing / do not mention it".
you-are-welcome.exampleSentence: Walang anuman po, masaya akong nakatulong sa inyo.

please.meaningNote: The polite prefix "paki-" (such as "pakikuha" or "pakidala") is also frequently used for requests.
please.exampleSentence: Pakiusap po, pakisuyo naman po ng baso.

excuse-me-pardon.meaningNote: Use "Makikiraan po" when asking to pass through; use "paumanhin" when apologizing.
excuse-me-pardon.exampleSentence: Makikiraan po sandali, kailangan ko lang lumabas.

goodbye-take-care.meaningNote: Polite farewell wishing the other person safety.
goodbye-take-care.exampleSentence: Paalam po, mag-iingat kayo sa inyong biyahe.

a-table-for-two-please.meaningNote: Polite request to a host or server when entering a restaurant.
a-table-for-two-please.exampleSentence: Magandang gabi po, mesa po para sa dalawa sa may bintana.

can-i-see-the-menu.text: Puwede po bang makahingi ng menu?
can-i-see-the-menu.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bahng mah-kah-HEENG-ee nahng MEH-nyoo
can-i-see-the-menu.meaningNote: Polite request for the list of available dishes.
can-i-see-the-menu.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang makahingi ng menu at listahan ng inumin?

what-do-you-recommend.text: Ano po ang specialty o masarap dito?
what-do-you-recommend.pronunciation: ah-NOH poh ahng SPEH-shahl-tee oh mah-sah-RAHP DEE-toh
what-do-you-recommend.meaningNote: Asking about the restaurant's specialty or best-selling dish.
what-do-you-recommend.exampleSentence: Bago lang po kami rito, ano po ang pinakamasarap na ulam dito?

the-check-please.text: Puwede na po bang makuha ang bill?
the-check-please.pronunciation: pweh-DEH nah poh bahng mah-KOO-hah ahng beel
the-check-please.meaningNote: In casual restaurants across the Philippines, saying "Bill out po" is also very common.
the-check-please.exampleSentence: Tapos na po kaming kumain, puwede na po bang makuha ang bill?

i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.text: May allergy po ako sa mani
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.pronunciation: my AH-lehr-jee poh ah-KOH sah mah-NEE
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.meaningNote: Important to tell the server immediately before your food is prepared.
i-am-allergic-to-peanuts.exampleSentence: Pakisabihan po ang kusina na may allergy po ako sa mani.

is-this-dish-spicy.text: Maanghang po ba ang pagkaing ito?
is-this-dish-spicy.pronunciation: mah-ahng-HAHNG poh bah ahng pahg-kah-EENG ee-TOH
is-this-dish-spicy.meaningNote: Asking whether the dish contains bird's eye chili (siling labuyo) or spicy ingredients.
is-this-dish-spicy.exampleSentence: Hindi po ako sanay sa sili, maanghang po ba ito?

water-without-ice-please.meaningNote: Request for room-temperature or unchilled water.
water-without-ice-please.exampleSentence: Medyo masama ang lalamunan ko, tubig na lang po na walang yelo.

delicious-compliment.meaningNote: Heartfelt compliment for the cook and kitchen staff.
delicious-compliment.exampleSentence: Napakasarap po ng pagkain, tiyak na babalik kami rito.

is-this-vegetarian.text: Wala po ba itong karne o isda?
is-this-vegetarian.pronunciation: wah-LAH poh bah ee-TOHNG kahr-NEH oh ees-DAH
is-this-vegetarian.meaningNote: Explicitly saying "no meat or fish" is clearer in the Philippines than simply saying "vegetarian".
is-this-vegetarian.exampleSentence: Gulay lang po ang kinakain ko, wala po ba itong halong karne?

can-i-have-this-to-go.meaningNote: Both "ipabalot" (have it wrapped) and "take-out" are commonly understood in the Philippines.
can-i-have-this-to-go.exampleSentence: Medyo marami pa pong natira, puwede po bang ipabalot ito?

where-is-the-bathroom.meaningNote: Restrooms are commonly called "banyo" or "CR" (Comfort Room) in the Philippines.
where-is-the-bathroom.exampleSentence: Mawalang-galang na po, saan po ang banyo rito?

how-do-i-get-to-the-station.text: Paano po pumunta sa istasyon ng tren?
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.pronunciation: pah-AH-noh poh poo-moon-TAH sah ees-tahs-YOHN nahng trehn
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.meaningNote: Asking for directions to a train station (such as the LRT, MRT, or commuter rail).
how-do-i-get-to-the-station.exampleSentence: Naliligaw po ako, paano po pumunta sa istasyon ng tren?

is-it-far-from-here.meaningNote: Checking whether a destination is walkable or requires taking a ride.
is-it-far-from-here.exampleSentence: Malayo po ba mula rito ang pamilihan kung lalakarin?

turn-left-at-the-corner.text: Kumaliwa po kayo pagdating sa kanto
turn-left-at-the-corner.pronunciation: koo-mah-lee-WAH poh kah-YOH pahg-dah-TEENG sah KAHN-toh
turn-left-at-the-corner.meaningNote: "Kumaliwa" is the verb for turning left.
turn-left-at-the-corner.exampleSentence: Kumaliwa po kayo pagdating sa kanto sa tapat ng botika.

turn-right-after-the-bank.text: Kumanan po kayo paglampas ng bangko
turn-right-after-the-bank.pronunciation: koo-MAH-nahn poh kah-YOH pahg-lahm-PAHS nahng BAHNG-koh
turn-right-after-the-bank.meaningNote: "Kumanan" is the verb for turning right using a landmark.
turn-right-after-the-bank.exampleSentence: Kumanan po kayo paglampas ng malaking bangko sa kanto.

go-straight-ahead.meaningNote: Continue walking in the same direction without turning.
go-straight-ahead.exampleSentence: Dire-diretso lang po kayo hanggang makita ninyo ang arko.

where-am-i-on-the-map.text: Nasaan po ako rito sa mapa?
where-am-i-on-the-map.pronunciation: nah-SAH-ahn poh ah-KOH REE-toh sah MAH-pah
where-am-i-on-the-map.meaningNote: Asking someone to point out your current location on a map.
where-am-i-on-the-map.exampleSentence: Medyo nalilito po ako, nasaan po ako rito sa mapa?

is-it-within-walking-distance.text: Kaya po bang lakarin mula rito?
is-it-within-walking-distance.pronunciation: KAH-yah poh bahng lah-kah-REEN MOO-lah REE-toh
is-it-within-walking-distance.meaningNote: Checking if the distance is short enough that you do not need public transit.
is-it-within-walking-distance.exampleSentence: Kaya po bang lakarin mula rito papunta sa museo?

where-is-the-bus-stop.text: Saan po ang sakayan ng bus o dyip?
where-is-the-bus-stop.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng sah-kah-YAHN nahng boos oh jeep
where-is-the-bus-stop.meaningNote: In the Philippines, travelers commonly ask for the bus or jeepney stop ("sakayan").
where-is-the-bus-stop.exampleSentence: Saan po ang sakayan ng bus papuntang kabayanan?

i-am-lost-can-you-help.text: Naliligaw po ako, puwede po bang magpatulong?
i-am-lost-can-you-help.pronunciation: nah-lee-lee-GOW poh ah-KOH, pweh-DEH poh bahng mahg-pah-TOO-lohng
i-am-lost-can-you-help.meaningNote: Polite request for help when you have lost your way.
i-am-lost-can-you-help.exampleSentence: Magandang araw po, naliligaw po ako, puwede po bang magpatulong?

where-is-baggage-claim.text: Saan po ang kuhanin ng bagahe?
where-is-baggage-claim.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng koo-HAH-neen nahng bah-GAH-heh
where-is-baggage-claim.meaningNote: Area where checked luggage is picked up at an airport or seaport.
where-is-baggage-claim.exampleSentence: Kakarating lang po namin, saan po ang kuhanin ng bagahe?

i-have-a-hotel-reservation.text: May reservation po ako sa pangalang ito
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.pronunciation: my reh-sehr-bahs-YOHN poh ah-KOH sah pah-NGAH-lahng ee-TOH
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.meaningNote: Spoken to the hotel front desk receptionist at check-in.
i-have-a-hotel-reservation.exampleSentence: Magandang hapon po, may reservation po ako sa pangalang Juan Cruz.

what-time-is-checkout.text: Anong oras po ang check-out bukas?
what-time-is-checkout.pronunciation: ah-NOHNG OH-rahs poh ahng chehk-owt BOO-kahs
what-time-is-checkout.meaningNote: Confirming the time by which you need to vacate your room.
what-time-is-checkout.exampleSentence: Anong oras po ang check-out bukas para maihanda ang gamit?

how-much-is-a-ticket-to.text: Magkano po ang pamasahe papuntang sentro?
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.pronunciation: mahg-KAH-noh poh ahng pah-mah-SAH-heh pah-poon-TAHNG SEHN-troh
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.meaningNote: "Pamasahe" refers to the fare for transportation such as a train, bus, or jeepney.
how-much-is-a-ticket-to.exampleSentence: Magkano po ang pamasahe papuntang kabayanan o sentro?

which-platform-for-the-airport.text: Saang platform po sasakay papuntang paliparan?
which-platform-for-the-airport.pronunciation: sah-AHNG PLAHT-fohrm poh sah-SAH-kye pah-poon-TAHNG pah-lee-PAH-rahn
which-platform-for-the-airport.meaningNote: "Paliparan" is the formal Filipino word for airport, though "airport" is also universally used.
which-platform-for-the-airport.exampleSentence: Saang platform po sasakay papuntang paliparan (airport)?

can-you-call-a-taxi.text: Puwede po ba ninyo akong tawagan ng taksi?
can-you-call-a-taxi.pronunciation: pweh-DEH poh bah neen-YOH ah-KOHNG tah-wah-GAHN nahng TAHK-see
can-you-call-a-taxi.meaningNote: Polite request asking a guard or receptionist to hail or book a taxi.
can-you-call-a-taxi.exampleSentence: Medyo maulan po, puwede po ba ninyo akong tawagan ng taksi?

do-you-have-wifi.text: May Wi-Fi po ba rito at ano po ang password?
do-you-have-wifi.pronunciation: my WAI-fai poh bah REE-toh aht ah-NOH poh ahng PAHS-wohrd
do-you-have-wifi.meaningNote: Everyday question at cafés, hotels, and guesthouses.
do-you-have-wifi.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang magtanong, may Wi-Fi po ba rito at ano ang password?

can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.text: Puwede ko po bang iwan muna ang aking bagahe nang ilang oras?
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.pronunciation: pweh-DEH koh poh bahng EE-wahn MOO-nah ahng AH-keeng bah-GAH-heh nahng EE-lahng OH-rahs
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.meaningNote: Polite request asking concierge or front desk staff to hold your bags temporarily.
can-i-leave-my-luggage-here.exampleSentence: Mamayang gabi pa po ang biyahe ko, puwede ko po bang iwan muna ang bagahe ko rito?

do-you-accept-credit-cards.text: Tumatanggap po ba kayo ng card o cash lang?
do-you-accept-credit-cards.pronunciation: too-mahn-tahng-GAHP poh bah kah-YOH nahng kahrd oh kahsh lahng
do-you-accept-credit-cards.meaningNote: Checking whether cash is required or if cards and e-wallets are accepted.
do-you-accept-credit-cards.exampleSentence: Bago po ako bumili, tumatanggap po ba kayo ng card o cash lang po?

where-can-i-exchange-currency.text: Saan po puwedeng magpapalit ng pera nang ligtas?
where-can-i-exchange-currency.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh pweh-DEHNG mahg-pah-pah-LEET nahng PEH-rah nahng leeg-TAHS
where-can-i-exchange-currency.meaningNote: Looking for an authorized money changer or bank to exchange foreign currency.
where-can-i-exchange-currency.exampleSentence: May dalang dolyar po ako, saan po puwedeng magpapalit ng pera nang ligtas?

help-me-please.text: Saklolo po! / Tulungan po ninyo ako!
help-me-please.pronunciation: sahk-LOH-loh poh / too-LOO-ngahn poh neen-YOH ah-KOH
help-me-please.meaningNote: "Saklolo" is the traditional urgent cry for help during an emergency.
help-me-please.exampleSentence: Saklolo po! Tulungan po ninyo ako, may magnanakaw!

call-an-ambulance.text: Tumawag po kayo ng ambulansya agad!
call-an-ambulance.pronunciation: too-MAH-wahg poh kah-YOH nahng ahm-boo-LAHN-syah AH-gahd
call-an-ambulance.meaningNote: Urgent request to bystanders during a serious accident or medical emergency.
call-an-ambulance.exampleSentence: May nawalan ng malay, tumawag po kayo ng ambulansya agad!

call-the-police.text: Tumawag po kayo ng pulis ngayon din!
call-the-police.pronunciation: too-MAH-wahg poh kah-YOH nahng poo-LEES ngah-YOHN deen
call-the-police.meaningNote: Calling for police assistance during a crime or dangerous situation.
call-the-police.exampleSentence: May nanggugulo po sa labas, tumawag po kayo ng pulis ngayon din!

where-is-the-nearest-hospital.text: Saan po ang pinakamalapit na ospital o klinika?
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh ahng pee-nah-kah-mah-LAH-peet nah ohs-pee-TAHL oh KLEE-nee-kah
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.meaningNote: Asking for the location of the closest hospital.
where-is-the-nearest-hospital.exampleSentence: Masama po ang pakiramdam ko, saan po ang pinakamalapit na ospital?

i-need-a-doctor.text: Kailangan ko po ng doktor ngayon din
i-need-a-doctor.pronunciation: kye-lah-NGAHN koh poh nahng dohk-TOHR ngah-YOHN deen
i-need-a-doctor.meaningNote: Requesting a medical doctor for an examination.
i-need-a-doctor.exampleSentence: Mataas po ang lagnat ng kasama ko, kailangan ko po ng doktor ngayon din.

where-is-a-pharmacy.text: Saan po may bukas na botika o parmasya?
where-is-a-pharmacy.pronunciation: sah-AHN poh my BOO-kahs nah boh-TEE-kah oh pahr-MAHS-yah
where-is-a-pharmacy.meaningNote: Pharmacies are commonly called "botika" or "drugstore" in the Philippines.
where-is-a-pharmacy.exampleSentence: Kailangan ko po ng gamot sa ubo, saan po may bukas na botika rito?

i-lost-my-passport.text: Nawala po ang aking pasaporte at pitaka
i-lost-my-passport.pronunciation: nah-wah-LAH poh ahng AH-keeng pah-sah-POHR-teh aht pee-TAH-kah
i-lost-my-passport.meaningNote: Should be reported immediately to the local police and your embassy.
i-lost-my-passport.exampleSentence: Naiwan ko po sa taksi kanina, nawala po ang aking pasaporte at pitaka.

i-cannot-breathe.meaningNote: Critical medical emergency requiring immediate air and medical attention.
i-cannot-breathe.exampleSentence: Pakiusap, bigyan ninyo ako ng espasyo, nahihirapan po akong huminga.

there-is-a-fire.text: May sunog po, lumikas na tayo sa gusali!
there-is-a-fire.pronunciation: my SOO-nohg poh, loo-MEE-kahs nah TAH-yoh sah goo-SAH-lee
there-is-a-fire.meaningNote: Urgent warning to evacuate immediately toward the fire exit.
there-is-a-fire.exampleSentence: May makapal na usok sa kusina, may sunog po, lumikas na tayo!

i-feel-very-dizzy.meaningNote: Warning sign of possible fainting or dehydration.
i-feel-very-dizzy.exampleSentence: Puwede po bang makahingi ng upuan? Nahihilo po ako at nanghihina.
